title: The Corentine Succession
problem: The death of Arbiter Vethara has left the Corentine Peninsula without a recognized authority to renew the bilateral treaties that have kept its five polities at peace for thirty years.
world: Five polities have coexisted under bilateral treaties ratified by the Arbiter, a title held for thirty years by Vethara of Corenth. The Arbiter held no army and claimed no territory; her authority rested on personal standing, the Conclave's ratification, and everyone's interest in having someone to call when things went wrong. She died twelve days ago and named no successor. The treaties have no renewal mechanism that all parties recognize.

map.name: Corenth
map.notes: The central city, seat of the old Arbiter, site of the Conclave's extraterritorial temple. Contested.

map.name: The Northern Passes
map.notes: Essaveth's territory between Caldrath and Corenth. Caldrath's army is camped at their foot; Corenth is three days' march beyond them.

map.name: Caldrath
map.notes: The kingdom's heartland, to the north.

map.name: Saivorn
map.notes: The coastal republic to the south, with the peninsula's only two deep-water ports. Reaches Corenth by sea.

map.name: The Southern Coast
map.notes: Merchant country with no single power; House Meranto's offices are here, but its leverage is everywhere.

turnZero: The treaties remain in force until they lapse unrenewed at the end of Turn 4 (the Crisis Clock's Breaking Point). Any faction may try to hasten or delay the lapse through action.
Caldrath's historical claim on Essaveth's northern province is dormant until Caldrath formally declares it.
The Conclave's extraterritorial status in Corenth derives from the treaties. If they lapse, it becomes contested.
Two mercenary companies operate on the peninsula. Both are expensive and in contact with more than one faction. Hiring one does not buy exclusivity.
unsettled: what the unpublished treaty clauses say

escalations.title: Blood at the passes
escalations.text: A Caldrath patrol and Essaveth's wardens clash at a gate tower; two men die. Each side names the other the aggressor.

escalations.title: Grain panic in Corenth
escalations.text: Bread prices double in a week. The city guilds petition for "a protector", and do not say whose.

escalations.title: Breaking Point: the treaties lapse
escalations.text: No renewal has been ratified. Every border, toll and debt guaranteed by the old order is now open to dispute, and the Conclave's temple is no longer clearly extraterritorial.

factions.name: Saivorn
factions.title: The Republic of Saivorn
factions.public: the peninsula's dominant commercial power; controls both major ports.

asPlayer.shortTerm: Prevent any military action that closes the peninsula's sea lanes before a new framework is established.
asPlayer.longTerm: Secure a successor treaty that guarantees commercial freedom of movement regardless of who holds political authority.
position: You control the only two deep-water ports on the peninsula. Any faction that needs to move goods or troops by sea needs your cooperation or your tolerance.
You have no standing army. Hired companies and a small patrol fleet defend the harbours; they cannot project power inland.
The Arbiter's death is, privately, not unwelcome. Her last treaty imposed tariff concessions that cost you considerably. You want a new order, not the old one restored.

bonus.name: The Harbour Writ
bonus.text: Open or close both ports to any cargo, at once and with full legal cover.

source.heading: Appendix A: The Corentine Succession (Solo) > The Republic of Saivorn

asAA.objective: Keep the sea lanes open and get commercial freedom written into whatever comes next

factions.name: Caldrath
factions.title: The Kingdom of Caldrath
factions.public: the strongest military force on the peninsula; has wanted more for a long time.

asPlayer.shortTerm: Establish a military presence in Corenth before any other faction does.
asPlayer.longTerm: Have the King of Caldrath recognized, by the Conclave or by sufficient consensus, as the new Arbiter or equivalent authority.
position: You have the largest standing army on the peninsula, camped at the foot of the northern passes. Through the passes, Corenth is three days' march away. Everyone knows this.
Five years ago, Vethara publicly rebuked Caldrath over a border dispute with Essaveth and ruled against you. The rebuke is in the Conclave's registers. It will be used against you.
Your military expansion was financed largely by loans from House Meranto. The debt is significant and the terms are not favourable.

bonus.name: The Old Muster Rolls
bonus.text: Call up the reserve levies: a second army, for one campaign.

source.heading: Appendix A: The Corentine Succession (Solo) > The Kingdom of Caldrath

asAA.objective: Put troops in Corenth first, then have the King recognized as Arbiter

factions.name: The Conclave
factions.title: The Conclave
factions.public: the religious body that ratified all the Arbiter's treaties; holds the originals.

asPlayer.shortTerm: Be formally recognized as the body that must ratify any new treaty framework or successor arrangement before it takes effect.
asPlayer.longTerm: Establish permanent Conclave oversight of whoever holds the Arbiter's role, however they are chosen.
position: You hold the original copies of all bilateral treaties, including clauses never made public. What is written there, and what you choose to reveal or withhold, is leverage.
Your temple complex in Corenth is extraterritorial. No faction can move against you there without the political cost of attacking a sacred institution.
You have no military force and are substantially in debt to House Meranto for a building programme not yet complete.

bonus.name: The Sealed Archive
bonus.text: Produce an original treaty document whose authenticity no one can credibly dispute.

source.heading: Appendix A: The Corentine Succession (Solo) > The Conclave

asAA.objective: Make Conclave ratification the price of any legitimate settlement
asAA.position: The treaty originals and an extraterritorial temple; no army; in debt to Meranto

secretTable: An unpublished clause grants Caldrath the northern province after thirty years, and the term has passed

factions.name: Essaveth
factions.title: The Principality of Essaveth
factions.public: a small border state whose existence was guaranteed by Vethara's last major treaty.

asPlayer.shortTerm: Secure a written guarantee of territorial integrity from at least two other factions before Caldrath's army moves.
asPlayer.longTerm: Have Essaveth's borders explicitly named and protected in whatever successor treaty emerges.
position: Your principality sits at the peninsula's crossroads. Caldrath's army cannot reach Corenth from the north without passing through or around your territory. This is your primary leverage and your primary vulnerability.
The Arbiter's last major treaty created your current borders. Without it, Caldrath has a historical claim on your northern province that predates Vethara's arbitration.
Your garrison is small but well positioned. You can hold your passes for weeks, not months. You need allies, and you need them before the army moves.

bonus.name: The Pass Wardens
bonus.text: Essaveth's hereditary gate-keepers: men who know every ledge and sally port. Scope: any action fought or enforced in the passes.

source.heading: Appendix A: The Corentine Succession (Solo) > The Principality of Essaveth

asAA.objective: Get its borders guaranteed in writing, by as many factions as possible

factions.name: House Meranto
factions.title: House Meranto
factions.public: a banking consortium with significant debts owed by every other faction.

asPlayer.shortTerm: Restructure or call in debts from at least two factions to improve your position before a new political order is settled.
asPlayer.longTerm: Have financial obligations explicitly protected, and the Meranto family's status as creditors formally recognised, in whatever treaty framework emerges.
position: You hold substantial debt from Caldrath, significant trade credits from Saivorn, and the Conclave's building programme. Every other faction owes you something.
You have no army, no territory, and no political claim. You can trigger a debt crisis that would damage every faction at once, including yourself.
Your agents are present in every major city. You often know things before the people they concern.

bonus.name: The Debt Clause
bonus.text: The emergency clause in Meranto's lending agreements: freeze a debtor's discretionary spending for thirty days.

source.heading: Appendix A: The Corentine Succession (Solo) > House Meranto
